facts.text: Coupon earned its name from the practice of paying workers in scrip, or coupons, during its early days as a company town.
Hikers near Coupon can reach the Horseshoe Curve and enjoy a rare view of the National Historic Landmark from a spot not visible at the visitor center.
Coupon is an unincorporated community in Cambria County, Pennsylvania, United States.
The community sits on the crest of the Allegheny Front, the eastern edge of the Allegheny Plateau, marking a dramatic rise in the landscape.
Coupon lies about 87 miles east of Pittsburgh and 9 miles west of Altoona, placing it midway between two larger Pennsylvanian cities.
At 2,342 feet above sea level, Coupon’s elevation gives it a cooler climate and sweeping views of the surrounding mountains.
